pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Fitzmaurice Primary School - Fitzmaurice Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Fitzmaurice Primary School
Welcome to Fitzmaurice Primary School part of the Palladian Academy Trust.
We are proud to be the Headteachers of this wonderful school where children and staff thrive.
Our child-centered therapeutic approach to learning ensures that all children are enabled to be successful. We know that emotionally happy and safe children learn best therefore our day is structured to ensure that children have the capacity to learn and achieve highly, regardless of their ability. As an inclusive school, we ensure that all children are successful and have a curriculum that matches their needs.
Whether your child loves music, sport, drama, history, or maths, your child will find that their passions are developed through our rich curriculum that is full of exciting learning opportunities. We have a specially enhanced curriculum offer called the Palladian Promise, which every child who is with us from Reception to Year 6 will experience many times. These activities have been carefully selected to ensure that every child experiences: trips to the beach, to London, stays away from home, and develops skills and knowledge that will stay with them throughout their life.
We hold the Healthy Schools Gold, Sports Mark Gold and the United Against Bullying Bronze awards, which recognise that holistic education is central to all that we do.
We have links throughout the community which enhance our children’s education.
The very best way to appreciate the education your child will receive at Fitzmaurice is to visit us. Please contact the office to arrange an appointment or visit us on an open day. We really hope that we will be meeting you in person soon.
Mr Simon Futcher, Executive Head
Mrs Jo Hill, Head of School

British Science Week 2026
Science Week is an exciting time for our pupils as they will explore the wonders of the world around them. Throughout the week, children will take part in fun experiments, hands-on investigations, and creative science challenges that help bring learning to life. From discovering how plants grow to exploring simple chemical reactions, pupils will show great curiosity and enthusiasm. Science Week encourages everyone to ask questions, think like scientists, and develop a love of discovery that we hope will continue long after the week has ended.

pageCache.pageTitle: Term 4 - Latest News - Fitzmaurice Primary School
pageCache.text:
Term 4
In Swift Class this term we have been learning about People and Places. Our Class Mouse Pip became lost and wrote us letters about where he might be and the children became brilliant cartographers making maps of places they know, the school and the classroom. During Science week Pip became a pirate and the children explored Floating and Sinking and made boats that would carry pirate treasure. We learned about what lives in the sea and explored how we could keep the sea clean to help all the creatures that live there. We have been exploring night and day and all the people who help us who have to work through the night, including midwives, policemen and doctors. We have been thinking about what things we love to do and writing about what jobs we might do when we are older. In maths we have been learning about how to split numbers into two parts and making part-whole models for numbers to 5. We have been amazing at learning our phonics and astounding everyone with our fabulous spelling! We also loved dressing up on World Book Day and talking about our favourite stories.
It has been a very exciting term in Wagtail class. The children really enjoyed participating in World book Day and it was lovely to see them dressed up as book characters. Science week was also very successful with everyone taking part in the experiment to investigate what happens to different materials when they are put in the ocean. The Year 1s have been busy writing instructions for jam sandwiches and fruit kebabs. Everyone really enjoyed making and then eating the kebabs! In Maths the Yr1s have been learning about addition and subtraction, they have been using some 'fancypants' vocabulary to describe their working-out which has been very impressive. The FS2 children have been learning to count to 20 starting on different numbers as well as continuing to work on partitioning 5. In Art all of the children have learnt the skill of paper rolling to create 3D pictures and then the amazing 3D spider that you can see hanging outside Wagtail class. In Geography the children have been learning about what it is like to live in Shanghai and comparing it to life in Bradford on Avon. There was a real split in the class between those who were keen to live in the busy city and those who prefer a quiet life in Wiltshire! They all enjoyed using Google Earth to locate different places and see how you would travel from one place to another.
This term, our Year 1 and 2 children have had an exciting and engaging time filled with creativity, curiosity and learning across the curriculum. We celebrated World Book Day by dressing up as our favourite book characters, sharing stories and developing a love of reading. During Science Week, the children became “curious chemists,” exploring what happens when materials are mixed through fun, hands on experiments such as making fluffy dough, creating explosive bicarbonate and vinegar reactions, and investigating colourful changes with a rainbow Skittles experiment. In English, the children used their new scientific knowledge about animals and their habitats to write imaginative explanation letters, explaining why it would be impossible to keep certain animals in unsuitable environments, such as penguins in bedrooms, sharks in baths, or giraffes in living rooms. It has been a fantastic term of discovery, creativity and enthusiasm for learning!
As we reach the end of term, Year 3 and 4 have so much to be proud of! One of the highlights was our fantastic performance of Dragon, where the children wowed us with their amazing singing, confident solos, and brilliant acting skills.
In English, inspired by our class book Varjak Paw, the children became journalists and wrote their own newspaper articles about missing cats. They showed great creativity while using direct and indirect speech, as well as rhetorical questions to engage their readers.
In Maths, the children have been working hard on fractions, including comparing fractions, converting improper fractions to mixed numbers, and placing fractions on number lines. They have also developed their understanding of mass, learning to read scales and convert between different units of measure.
In Science, pupils explored pulls and pushes and magnetism, we also enjoyed an exciting Science Day, based on our topic on forces.
It has been a wonderful term full of enthusiasm, curiosity, and achievement - well done to all our pupils!
Term 4 was an engaging term for us all in Year 5 & 6. We explored the fascinating world of deserts, discussed their environments, and considered whether we would enjoy living in one. In Science, we built on last term’s learning with a new focus on planets and the phases of the Moon. Our class book was Can You See Me?, a thoughtful story about an autistic girl named Tally that encouraged empathy and understanding. During Science Week, the children took part in a range of exciting investigations and experiments, including designing and testing straw rockets and pop rockets. They enjoyed exploring how forces affect movement, making predictions, testing their ideas, and evaluating their results. We also celebrated World Book Day, dressing up and sharing stories with younger year groups.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pencelli 2026 - Latest News - Fitzmaurice Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pencelli 2026
Our Year 6 pupils had an amazing time during their week-long residential trip to Pencelli. Throughout the week, they took part in a wide range of exciting outdoor activities, including canoeing, climbing, exploring a dingle, and even sliding down waterfalls!
The children showed fantastic teamwork and resilience as they supported one another through challenging activities, including navigating caves together. It was wonderful to see their confidence grow as they encouraged their friends and worked together to overcome obstacles.
As well as developing their adventurous spirit, the pupils also built important life skills. They packed their own lunches each day and took increasing responsibility for their personal belongings, helping to develop their independence throughout the week.
We are incredibly proud of how the children represented our school. Their enthusiasm, determination, and positive attitudes made the trip a memorable experience for everyone involved. Well done, Year 6!

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast & After School Club - Fitzmaurice Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Club
At Fitzmaurice, we offer child care provision for children before and after school, together with a range of school clubs.
Term Time Child Care Provision
School offers an Early Morning Club from 7.45 am - 8.40 am with the option of breakfast which can be booked through school via Arbor.
Along side this we offer an After School Club with an external provider JAG.
A brilliant start and finish to the school day
The new school year is here, and JAG’s Ofsted-registered after school clubs are back – giving children a fun, active and engaging place to finish their school day.
For 2026/27, we’ve upgraded our Adventure Programme too, with new activities, new themes and even more for children to get stuck into at our Stay And Play after school clubs.
NEW: Play Your Way & Sound Safari
This half term brings two new themes: first up is Play Your Way, followed by Sound Safari – with fresh activities to get children creating, moving, playing and discovering together.
Snack Lab Takeover Mondays
Mondays just got tastier! This term, our Toastie Takeover is giving snack time an upgrade, with warm, golden toasties and tasty fillings to discover.
Team Up Fridays – First Up: Baseball!
There’s something new to get stuck into each half term with Team Up Fridays.
First up is Baseball! Every Friday this half term, children can practise the basics, get active and play together – building confidence and teamwork while having plenty of fun.
Flexible childcare that works around family life
Whether you need the same days every week or just need an occasional session, JAG makes before and after school childcare easy to fit around your family.
Recurring Bookings – Secure your regular days for the academic year and spread the cost monthly.
Ad-Hoc Bookings – Book when you need us, up to 8 weeks in advance and subject to availability.
You may also be able to use Tax-Free Childcare and other eligible funding support towards the cost of your sessions.

Current Governors
The Governing Body exists to provide strategic oversight to the way the school is run and to be accountable for the decisions made by it. We have one over-riding purpose: to help make Fitzmaurice the best place for our children to learn.
Details of attendance and terms of office can be found at the bottom of the page.
Simon Futcher - Executive Headteacher Simon Futcher - Ex Officio - Executive Headteacher
I have the enormous privilege of being the Executive Headteacher across Fitzmaurice Primary School, Westwood with Iford Primary School and Churchfields, the Village School. All schools are proud members of Palladian Academy Trust.
I have worked in a number of schools and taught every primary age group from nursery to year six. Before taking up my current role in January 2024, I have had substantial successful experience as both a Headteacher and Deputy Headteacher of small village and large city schools.
I have also served as a governor in many schools for a period exceeding twenty years so am fully aware that the relationship between the governing body and leadership team is pivotal for ensuring the ongoing success of any school. This takes the form of the Local Governing Committee being a ‘critical friend’ to support yet challenge the leadership team to ensure we provide the best possible education for our pupils.
Fran Stevens - Trust Board Appointed Governor - Chair of Governors
Fran has a background in education, having worked as a secondary school teacher for twelve years, before having children. She joins the Governing Body for Weswood with Iford and Fiztmaurice Primary Schools as a Parent Governor, as her two children now attend Fitzmaurice Primary. Having moved to Bradford on Avon in 2017, Fran is passionate about cooking and food writing. She is a recipe writer for a Wiltshire-based magazine, as well as running her own food blog. More generally, she works as a copywriter.
Abigail Thorpe - Trust Board Appointed Governor - Vice Chair
Abigail is delighted to have joined as a Community Governor for Fitzmaurice and Westwood and Iford Primary schools. She has a daughter who attends Fitzmaurice Primary School and after a career as a Primary school teacher, she now works as a private tutor, teaching children online internationally. Abigail and her family have lived in the local area for five years, following eight years in New Zealand.
Liz Parry - Community Governor
Liz Parry has been a governor of Fitzmaurice Primary school since 2022 and Westwood with Iford since the Local Governing committee combined.
Liz has lived in Bradford on Avon for ten years and is a local General Practitioner and parent to three children who all attend Fitzmaurice Primary School.
Alex Ladnor - Staff Governor
Alex Ladner is new to the governor’s team, starting this year and joins as a staff member from Fitzmaurice school.
He is in his third year of teaching at Fitzmaurice having recently passed his ECT last year.
Abby Kean - Parent Governor
I am a Parent Governor with a child in Year 5 at Fitzmaurice. I worked in secondary education as a science teacher for twenty years. I now run a Counselling practice in Bradford on Avon and Bath working with children, young people and adults.
Jo Holden - Parent Governor
Jo joined the governing body in 2025 and is a proud parent of a child attending Fitzmaurice. She is committed to supporting the school community to ensure every pupil has the opportunity to thrive and enjoy their primary education. She has lived in the local area for nearly five years and works as a communications consultant.
Jo Hill - Associate Governor - Head of School FPS
Jo has been working at Fitzmaurice since September 2012 as the Deputy Headteacher. She has been Head of School since September 2022. Jo has over 30 years teaching experience and has taught every primary age group from reception to year 6.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brilliant maths - Latest News - Fitzmaurice Primary School
pageCache.text:
Brilliant maths
This week there has been lots of brilliant maths learning across the school.
In year 2, the children have been learning to use the terms 'heavier' and 'lighter' when describing the mass of objects. They enjoyed being human balance scales.
In year 3 the children have been learning to choose efficient strategies to add and subtract to solve word problems. They have been learning to look for near doubles, use known number facts and bridge across 10 and 100.
In year 6 the children have been learning about prime numbers and how to multiply a number by 100.
Well done to all the children for their brilliant effort this week!

pageCache.pageTitle: Eggciting Times in Swift Class - Latest News - Fitzmaurice Primary School
pageCache.text:
Eggciting Times in Swift Class
We have been so lucky in Swift Class as parents Anna and Jim from Stowford Manor Farm have provided us with everything we needed to hatch chicks from eggs! We learned about: the role of an incubator; candling the eggs to see if there is a chick inside; the pipping stage where little holes appear; and finally the joy of hatching chicks themselves! We were incredibly lucky to get six chicks from six eggs and absolutely loved talking to the chicks and admiring how quickly they fluffed up and began exploring the world.

twitterTweet this page
Our Curriculum
At Fitzmaurice Primary School, pupils benefit from a broad, rich and exciting curriculum that develops both knowledge and skills. Our curriculum is carefully designed to be relevant to children’s interests, inspire enjoyment, nurture creativity and independence, and challenge every learner to achieve their full potential. We strive to provide engaging learning opportunities that appeal to and motivate all children.
One of the strengths of our curriculum is the exceptional range of experiences we offer beyond the classroom. Through special events, educational visits, visitors, extracurricular activities and strong community links, children are given opportunities to enrich and extend their learning in meaningful and memorable ways. Previous highlights have included Science Week, visits to We The Curious, The Roman Baths, Westonbirt, Lyme Regis and London, where pupils enjoyed seeing The Lion King. Children also participate in the West Wiltshire Dance Festival and residential visits to Charterhouse and Plas Pencelli.
A visit to any classroom at Fitzmaurice will reveal engaging, purposeful learning experiences that foster curiosity, confidence, independence and critical thinking. Learning environments throughout the school, from Reception to Year 6, are stimulating and designed to support high-quality learning. Throughout the year, pupils enjoy a wide variety of educational visits, inspiring visitors, community projects and opportunities to collaborate with children across different year groups.
During teachers’ planning, preparation and assessment (PPA) time, pupils take part in a range of specialist-led enrichment activities, including Forest School, swimming, physical education and music. In Key Stage 2, all children learn to play the ukulele and develop their singing skills as part of the music curriculum. Pupils who learn musical instruments are regularly given opportunities to showcase their talents through performances and special assemblies.
We are also proud to offer a wide range of extracurricular clubs before and after school. These vary throughout the year and include both free and paid activities. Popular clubs have included Art, Netball, Active Club and Choir. Our sports teams consistently achieve success and provide pupils with valuable opportunities to develop teamwork, resilience and confidence.
For further information about what your child is learning, please visit the relevant class page. If you have any questions about our curriculum, please contact your child’s class teacher. Visitors to the school website are welcome to contact the school office for additional information.
